The redirect point holds. I took it from the code, not from loading the page. page-claim:allow

`app/api/client/login/route.ts:39` always sends a successful login to `/client/<slug>`. The login page only reads `c`, `e` and `sent` from the URL (`app/client/login/page.tsx:20`), so there's no way to pass "return to /partners". Someone bounced from /partners signs in and lands on their own workspace instead.

I haven't run it in a browser. That's partly because no /partners page exists yet, so a signed-in visit would still show a 404.

To send people back to /partners after login, the login form and route would need a checked `next` parameter that only accepts paths on this site, so it can't be used to redirect people to another site. That's about 15 lines across the page and the route. I haven't made that change.
